scenarios.title: Journal deleted after a crash
scenarios.expected: a deleted journal is indistinguishable from a fresh repository: reconcile reports RECONCILED with nothing pending
scenarios.notes: Observation, P2: the durable record is the only witness; deleting it (or losing it) removes the pending intent from recovery. No ref was moved in this scenario, so no double publication results; after a crash-after-ref the second publish is ALREADY_PUBLISHED. Recorded as an honest limitation, not a gate breach.

scenarios.title: Valid-JSON non-object journal line
scenarios.expected: a valid-JSON but non-object journal line is silently ignored: reconcile says RECONCILED
scenarios.notes: Observation, P3: `read_journal` refuses lines that fail to parse (torn writes), but a syntactically valid non-object line (or an object without fields) is accepted and counted as nothing. No invariant is broken with the records Flow itself writes; recorded for completeness.

scenarios.title: Crafted two intents with two outcomes
scenarios.expected: a hand-crafted journal with two intents and two outcomes is accepted as reconciled
scenarios.notes: Observation, P3: the counting rule is intentionally mechanical; a writer who can already rewrite the journal can synthesize a balanced history. Not reachable through Flow's own append path (ids carry a nanosecond suffix).
